fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Exodus hides a mother nobody names. Chance Garton and Dylan Saccoccio track Pharaoh's daughter through Jubilees and Josephus to the name Maris, sea-born like the Virgin Mary, then map the infant Moses onto the stars through a coin of Philip the Arab, a Renaissance painting read as a star chart, and the case that Noah himself never appears in any record before the Middle Ages.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: The second hour tackles the burning bush story, fire as a divine mediator and messenger, baptism and its analogs, Moses' identity as one of the Muses, and the ancient system of the astrological Naros Cycle and messianic incarnations.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Fire as the Mediator Between Man and God", "body": "The burning bush is treated here not as a single miracle but as one expression of a doctrine the priesthoods carried everywhere. Exodus and Leviticus command that the lamp burn always and that the fire on the altar never go out, Herodotus describes Persians climbing the loftiest summits to sacrifice to Jupiter, the name they give to the whole circuit of the firmament, Zoroastrian liturgy calls fire the son of Ahura Mazda, and the Greek Hestia and Roman Vesta keep a hearth that must never die. Fire becomes divine presence, cosmic principle, and the channel carrying prayer upward."}, {"title": "Moses as Water and Moses as Fire", "body": "Vedic hymns say the gods discovered Agni in the midst of waters, and other passages give wood rather than flame as his origin, so making fire is drawing out an invisible principle of life already present in matter. That is offered as the idea behind a bush that burns without being consumed. If Moses is the Nile, he is the visible current that sustains Egypt and in flooding both destroys and preserves. Water is the manifestation of life and fire the hidden source, and without one the other either freezes solid or scorches the world bare."}, {"title": "Robert Taylor and the Religion of Water", "body": "Taylor is read at length asking why every believer must be ducked, dipped, sprinkled or born of water before entering the kingdom. Christ is called the fountain of living waters, tells Peter that without washing he has no part in him, meets the woman of Samaria standing directly over the well like a pump, has a voice as the sound of many waters, and cannot die on the cross until water is let out of him. Moses in the cloud and Moses in the sea become the waters above and the waters below."}, {"title": "The Ark, the Temple and the Marked Off Sky", "body": "Temple is traced to the Latin templum, a portion of sky marked off by the augurs, which lets the ark double as a temple rather than a boat. Jacob Bryant is quoted saying the ancients esteemed the ark an emblem of the system of the heavens, which explains why emperors would wear Noah as a title of rulership on their coinage. Martianus Capella describes a ship laden with blessed merchandise and seven presiding sailor brothers, and Egyptian deities sail the sea of stars on solar barks, the same word as the tree bark written on."}, {"title": "The Neros Cycle and Moses as Muse", "body": "Higgins names a roughly six hundred year cycle of destruction and regeneration, and in modern Greek nero means water, while the laws of Manu call the waters Nara. Every cycle had its song, its muse and its savior, so Moses saving the Hebrews and writing their story down makes him the muse who preserves the messiah. Salivahana appears nine times in Indian records with nearly the same history, the Curetes guard the infant Zeus on Mount Ida, and Kouros simply means youth. The caution offered is that the Neros itself may be a Renaissance invention."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text": "This was the same story dressed differently for different peoples, whether it was Moses as the savior, Bacchus as the savior, or Jesus as the savior, depending on where you're at.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Fire is a divine presence and a cosmic principle that must be ritually preserved.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Latin comes from Etruscan. It doesn't come from Greek as pretended. It's a lingua franca of the ancient Italian cultures, and it's observable that Sanskrit comes from Latin.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "If Moses is the Nile or simply water, he is the visible embodiment of life in Egypt, a stream that sustains and nourishes, and in flooding, both destroys and preserves.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Moses as Nile and Moses at the bush are two ways of describing the same thing.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The ark, the archon, the all-father, the all-in-one, that to me is the best way to categorize all of it.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "If you see big significant events hitting at around 600 years apart from each other, it doesn't have to be exact, you can probably guess that those are the fingerprints of mythology, not real history.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Moses is the author of the Hebrew Salvation in a double sense. He saves them from Egypt and preserves their story by writing it down, allegedly.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The problem is when people talk about these subjects, they gloss over the fact that they just assume it's ancient when I'm showing them it's not.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I think that this globalism project has been going on for a long time, but it had better compartmentalization, and so the modern version of globalism has become more and more uniform.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
fields.Title: Moses and Jesus Share the Same Mother: Maris and the Astro-Theology of Exodus
